definition: TensorFlow Hub (also styled TF Hub) is an open-source machine learning library and online repository that provides TensorFlow model components, called modules.
details: It is maintained by Google as part of the TensorFlow ecosystem and allows developers to discover, publish, and reuse pretrained models for tasks such as computer vision, natural language processing, and transfer learning.

explainer.lead: TensorFlow Hub is an open-source library and online repository providing reusable TensorFlow model components called modules. It matters because it lets developers discover, publish and reuse pretrained models rather than training from scratch.

tiers.eli5: It is an app store for pieces of pretrained AI models that you can drop into your own project.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pull pretrained modules for computer vision, NLP and transfer learning, then fine-tune them on their own data. The pitfall is that reused modules carry their original preprocessing assumptions, which must match your inputs.
tiers.paperLevel: Maintained by Google within the TensorFlow ecosystem; provides TensorFlow modules for discovery, publication and reuse across tasks including computer vision, natural language processing and transfer learning. Quality and compatibility depend on the contributed module.

explainer.example: A developer wanting an image classifier retrieves a pretrained vision module from TensorFlow Hub and adapts it to a new dataset through transfer learning.
